data.name: About_Description
data.value: Zabbix Monitor shows the state of your Zabbix server in the Windows notification area. The color of the tray icon tells you at a glance whether everything is OK or whether there are warnings or errors. The tooltip and the problems window list the current problems; from the problems window you can acknowledge or suppress them and open the Zabbix dashboard.

data.name: Help_GettingStarted_Text
data.value: 1. Open Settings (right-click the tray icon > Settings). 2. Enter the Zabbix URL, for example https://zabbix.example.com. If Zabbix runs in a subdirectory, include it, for example https://example.com/zabbix. 3. Enter an API token. You create it in Zabbix under User settings > API tokens. 4. Click Test to check the connection and the API token, then Save.

data.name: Help_Tray_Text
data.value: • Green: no problems. Yellow: warnings. Red: errors, or the server cannot be reached. Gray: not loaded yet. • Hover over the icon to see a summary of the current problems. • Left-click opens the problems window. • Right-click opens the menu with Refresh, Settings, Help, About and Exit.

data.name: Help_Problems_Text
data.value: • Shows the current problems, sorted by severity and time. The colored bar marks errors (E) and warnings (W). • ⟳ refreshes the list, ⌂ opens the Zabbix dashboard. Clicking a problem also opens the dashboard. • Right-click a problem > Edit alarm to acknowledge or suppress it.

data.name: Help_Alarms_Text
data.value: • Acknowledge only: marks the problem as acknowledged in Zabbix and adds your message. • Suppress for 5 minutes to 1 day, or until a chosen time: acknowledges the problem and hides it until then. • The message field at the top of the menu is prefilled with the default message from the settings and can be changed for each action. • Suppressed problems are hidden unless "Keep showing suppressed problems" is enabled in the settings. • The Zabbix user of the API token needs permission to acknowledge and suppress the events.

data.name: Help_Settings_Text
data.value: • Zabbix URL: address of the Zabbix web interface, including a subdirectory if there is one. The API path /api_jsonrpc.php is added automatically. • Dashboard URL: page opened by ⌂ and by clicking a problem. If empty, the Zabbix URL is used. • API token: stored in the Windows Credential Manager, never in the configuration file. When a token is stored, the field shows asterisks; enter a new token only to replace it. • Ignore SSL certificate errors: only for testing, see Security. • Dark mode: dark or light colors for all windows. • Language: System uses the Windows display language (English if it is not supported). The change applies right after saving. • Poll interval: how often problems are loaded, at least 10 seconds. • Tooltip delay: how long the mouse must rest on the tray icon before the summary appears (0 to 10000 ms). • Warning and error threshold: see Severities. • Keep showing suppressed problems: also list problems that are suppressed in Zabbix. • Refresh automatically after acknowledging/suppressing: reload the list after an alarm action. • Default message: text prefilled in the alarm menu. • Windows Credential Manager: name (target) and user name under which the token is stored. Change them only if your organization requires specific names. • Check for updates automatically: check for a new version every 6 hours, see Updates.

data.name: Help_Severities_Text
data.value:
Zabbix uses six severities: 0 Not classified, 1 Information, 2 Warning, 3 Average, 4 High, 5 Disaster.
• Problems below the warning threshold are ignored. • From the warning threshold up to the error threshold they count as warnings (yellow). • From the error threshold on they count as errors (red).
Defaults: warning threshold 2, error threshold 4, so 0-1 ignored, 2-3 warning, 4-5 error. The error threshold must be higher than the warning threshold.

data.name: Help_Security_Text
data.value: • The API token is sent with every request. Use https:// for the Zabbix URL; for http:// the application asks for confirmation when saving, because the token would be readable on the network. • Ignore SSL certificate errors turns off the check of the server certificate. An attacker on the network could then pretend to be your Zabbix server and steal the token. Instead, import the server certificate or your own certification authority into the trusted certificates of Windows. • Use a dedicated Zabbix user for the token with as few permissions as possible: read access to the host groups you want to monitor and, if you want to edit alarms, permission to acknowledge and suppress problems. • The token is stored encrypted for your Windows user in the Credential Manager. • Network connections: the application only connects to the Zabbix server from the settings and, every 6 hours, to GitHub (api.github.com) to check for a new version. No token and no data from Zabbix is sent to GitHub. The check can be turned off in the settings.

data.name: Help_Troubleshooting_Text
data.value: • The tray icon is red and the tooltip shows an error: open Settings and check the Zabbix URL and the API token with Test. • Error mentioning a certificate or SSL: Windows does not trust the server certificate, see Security. • "Not authorized" or a permission error: the token has expired, was deleted in Zabbix, or its user lacks permissions. Create a new token and enter it in Settings. • A problem from Zabbix is missing: check the warning threshold and whether the problem is suppressed. Problems of disabled triggers, hosts or items are not shown, just like in the Zabbix frontend. • Configuration file: %AppData%\ZabbixTrayMonitor\config.json. It contains all settings except the token. If it cannot be read, a copy is saved as config.corrupt.json and default settings are used. The About window has a link to the folder.

data.name: Help_Install_Text
data.value:
The application needs the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64). Every release contains: • ...-setup.exe (recommended): checks whether the runtime is installed, downloads and installs it from Microsoft only if it is missing, then installs the application. • ...-runtime-dependent.msi: small installer for scripts, Intune or Group Policy where the runtime is deployed separately. It does not install without the runtime. • ...-win-x64.msi: larger installer with the runtime included, also for computers without internet access. • ZIP files: portable versions without installation and without autostart, with or without the runtime.
The installers install the application for all users to C:\Program Files\ZabbixTrayMonitor, add a Start menu shortcut and start the application when a user signs in. Administrator rights are required. At the end of an interactive installation you can choose to start the application right away. • Silent installation: msiexec /i <file>.msi /qn, or <file>-setup.exe /quiet • Without autostart: add AUTOSTART=0 to the msiexec command. • Group Policy: assign the MSI to computers under Computer Configuration > Policies > Software Settings > Software installation. It is installed at the next restart. • Update: install the new version; the old version is replaced and a running instance is closed first. • Uninstall: Settings > Apps > Zabbix Monitor. Your settings and the API token are kept, the .NET runtime stays installed.

data.name: Help_Updates_Text
data.value: • Every 6 hours (and one minute after the start) the application checks on GitHub whether a new version has been released. If there is one, a notification appears next to the tray icon and the tray menu shows "Update available". • The update window shows the installed and the new version. Download opens the release page; run the installer from there to update. Skip this version hides the notice until an even newer version is released. Later reminds you at the next check. • With "Install updates automatically" in the settings, a new version is downloaded, checked and installed after a confirmation by Windows; otherwise it is only shown. Install in the update window does the same at once. The installer must have the correct checksum and be signed with the certificate of the project, otherwise it is not installed. The portable ZIP version is only notified. • Without this setting, nothing is downloaded or installed automatically. Only the number of the latest version is requested from GitHub (api.github.com). • About > Check for updates checks right away. The About window also shows the time and the result of the last check, including errors of the automatic check. • The automatic check can be turned off in Settings. Administrators can turn it off for all users with the registry value DisableUpdateCheck = 1 (DWORD) under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Policies\ZabbixTrayMonitor.
